f6b16b2b6f5c.tr: Logistic regression multiplies features by weights and adds them into a linear score, then feeds that score into an S-shaped curve called the sigmoid to turn it into a probability between 0 and 1. If the probability exceeds a set threshold (usually 0.5), it assigns that class. It works with a single straight line, but because it answers in probabilities, it also tells you "how sure it is".

6746aeece814.tr: z = w·x + b is exactly the formula 5-2 linear regression builds. What it regresses is the log-odds of the probability; what it does with the result is classification.
